full_judgment:
4. The defendants filed written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit was not maintainable and raised several other objections as to valuation, court fee etc. They further alleged that the suit was not maintainable in the absence of a prayer for recovery of khas possession. The defendants contended that the plaintiffs acquired no title in the suit property on the basis of the so-called oral gift which is an afterthought and concocted with ulterior motive for illegal gains. They further contended that section 23 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949 is a bar to the accrual of title to the plaintiffs in the suit property in the absence of a registered written instrument of conveyance. They further contended that even if the gift was genuine as contemplated under Mohammaden Law no title did pass upon the plaintiffs in the absence of a registered written instrument of gift. They, however, stoutly denied the story of the alleged oral gift and contended that the application before the Income Tax Authority for clearance certificate is a manipulated affair. They contended that Abdur Rahman Chowdhury died without making any gift and that the defendants being consanguine paternal uncles of the donor (sons of the consanguine brothers of the grandfather of deceased Abdur Rahman Chowdhury) are entitled to 6 annas share by inheritance under the Mohammaden Law. But the plaintiffs have set up the case of verbal gift to defeat the claim of these defendants in the disputed property and that the suit ought to be dismissed and the succession certificate should be granted to the defendants. The facts relating to the succession case need not be stated separately since the defendants defence in this suit is their case as petitioners in the succession certificate case. This suit was tried analogously along with the said Succession Certificate Case. 

 16. In the background of the evidence let us consider whether Haji Abdur Rahman Choudhury made declaration of oral gift in presence of the witnesses as alleged and whether the said gift was accepted by the plaintiffs and delivery of possession of the disputed property was given. In this connection it may be mentioned that the disputed property is in possession of the tenant under an agreement of tenancy. It is in evidence that the plaintiff No. 1 is the widow and plaintiff No. 2 is the only daughter and only issue of late Abdur Rahman Choudhury. It appears that late Abdur Rahman Choudhury left no near relation besides the plaintiffs. The defendants are step-brothers of, grandfather of late Abdur Rahman Choudbury. It is not disputed that the defendants are distant agnates and that they would inherit a share of the property left by Abdur Rahman Choudhury if there was no disposition of the suit property by the impugned oral gift. The plaintiffs have filed this suit for declaration of their title on the basis of oral gift. We do not think that the plaintiffs are required to pay ad valorem court fee as they were not seeking recovery of khas possession after establishment of their title. The relief for declaration is competent and as such the suit as framed is maintainable.
